S1.rationale: Agency Swarm Agent runs a model/tool/action feedback loop. Independently discovered upstream issue #828 reports traces sent to api.openai.com while model calls use an overridden base URL; this is a first-party integration problem, NOT an S1 autonomy finding in Index. The narrow tracing-egress hypothesis is assessment-informed.

S2.rationale: Communication flows, SendMessage delegation and Handoff exchange work, but the reviewed ToolConcurrencyManager serializes tools inside one agent rather than competing sibling S1 resources. No native inter-agent contention demand appears in the bounded issue check.

S3.rationale: An Agency can compose multiple agents and shared context yet no first-party portfolio authority owns live commitments and resource reallocation. Model/tool delegation alone does not establish a desired whole-Agency controller or product need for one.

S3*.rationale: Developer guardrails validate ordinary inputs/outputs but do not use independent operational evidence and corrective return to S3. The reported tracing endpoint issue is not a correctness auditor defect; no separate review candidate is supported here.

S4.rationale: External tools, model plans, memory and persistence support current work rather than decisions to adopt future organizational capabilities. No concrete user-requested long-horizon adaptation flow was verified in this bounded assessment review.

S5.rationale: Developers choose agent topology, instructions and guardrails, and runtime hooks enforce them for calls. No credible identity-level conflict resolution mechanism or first-party policy expansion demand is evidenced by the checked source.
